# TimelineGroup { #timetoalign.timelines.TimelineGroup }

```python
timelines.TimelineGroup(
    id=None,
    name=None,
    timelines=None,
    meta=None,
    styling=None,
)
```

An array of timelines sharing one graphical start and end point.

By definition every member's 0 coincides with every other member's 0 and
every member's length with every other member's length; a position in
between converts linearly. Position ``p`` on member A is
``p · len_B / len_A`` on member B, computed exactly — a float enters as
its exact dyadic ``Fraction`` — and written in B's declared number type.

When only part of a timeline participates, the participant is a child of
that timeline: the child carries its exact offset, and the child is the
member. A member is never placed partially.

A member may be of unknown length: membership states that it shares the
group's start and end, wherever that end lies. Carrying a position
between two members needs both lengths, so such a conversion raises
``UnknownLengthError``; one member's length is never carried to another.

Members keep the order in which they were added.

## Attributes {.doc-section .doc-section-attributes}

| Name    | Type                                                | Description                                                                                                                                       |
|---------|-----------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| id      | [str](`str`)                                        | Unique identifier for this group, ``group_N`` unless given.                                                                                       |
| name    | [str](`str`) \| None                                | Optional human-readable name.                                                                                                                     |
| meta    | [dict](`dict`)\[[str](`str`), [Any](`typing.Any`)\] | Additional metadata dictionary.                                                                                                                   |
| styling | [dict](`dict`)\[[str](`str`), [Any](`typing.Any`)\] | The members of the manifest's ``graphical`` other than ``order`` (``styles``, ``statements`` and any other), kept as given and never interpreted. |

## Examples {.doc-section .doc-section-examples}

```python
>>> from fractions import Fraction
>>> from timetoalign.timelines import TimelineGroup
>>> from timetoalign.timelines.types import (
...     ContinuousLogicalTimeline,
...     DiscreteGraphicalTimeline,
... )
>>> score = ContinuousLogicalTimeline(length=Fraction(16))
>>> image = DiscreteGraphicalTimeline(length=4800)
>>> group = TimelineGroup(timelines=[score, image])
>>> group.id, group.timeline_ids
('group_1', ['clt_1', 'dgt_1'])
>>> group.get_coordinate_at(Fraction(1, 3), "clt_1", format="coordinate")
Coordinate(Fraction(1, 3), quarters)
>>> group.get_timestamp_at(Fraction(1, 3), "clt_1").get_coordinate_for(
...     "dgt_1", format="int"
... )
100
```

### add_timeline { #timetoalign.timelines.TimelineGroup.add_timeline }

```python
timelines.TimelineGroup.add_timeline(timeline)
```

Add a member; its whole extent ``[0, length]`` spans the group.

A member's 0 coincides with every other member's 0 and its length
with every other member's length. To let only part of a timeline
participate, add the child of that timeline covering the part.

Every timeline id in the newcomer's manifest tree (its root and all
that root's descendants) must be free in the group's trees.

A newcomer that is an ancestor or a descendant of a member is
refused: a child sits at its offset inside its parent, so the two
cannot share one start and end. Every check runs before anything
changes, so a refused newcomer is left as it was.

#### Parameters {.doc-section .doc-section-parameters}

| Name     | Type         | Description                   | Default    |
|----------|--------------|-------------------------------|------------|
| timeline | \'Timeline\' | The timeline or child to add. | _required_ |

#### Raises {.doc-section .doc-section-raises}

| Name   | Type                       | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
|--------|----------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
|        | [ValueError](`ValueError`) | If the timeline is already a member; if it is nested with a member; or if a given id of its tree — its own, its root's or any descendant's — is held by another timeline of the group's trees or is the group's given id (a minted id held there is minted again instead, and a minted group id that a newcomer's given id takes is minted again). |

#### Examples {.doc-section .doc-section-examples}

```python
>>> from timetoalign.timelines import TimelineGroup
>>> from timetoalign.timelines.types import (
...     ContinuousPhysicalTimeline,
...     DiscreteGraphicalTimeline,
... )
>>> image = DiscreteGraphicalTimeline(length=5000)
>>> holes = DiscreteGraphicalTimeline(length=2000)
>>> image.add_child(holes, offset=1000)
>>> group = TimelineGroup(timelines=[ContinuousPhysicalTimeline(length=8.0)])
>>> group.add_timeline(holes)
>>> group.get_coordinate_at(2.0, "cpt_1")
IdCoordinate(2.0, seconds, 'cpt_1')
>>> group.get_timestamp_at(2.0, "cpt_1").get_coordinate_for("dgt_2", format="int")
500
```

### apply_flow { #timetoalign.timelines.TimelineGroup.apply_flow }

```python
timelines.TimelineGroup.apply_flow(
    flow,
    flow_controller,
    reference_timeline_id,
    *,
    include_children=True,
    name=None,
)
```

Unfold ALL timelines in this group via a single flow.

Uses the flow controller's repeat structure to compute section
boundaries in the reference timeline's coordinate space, then
resolves those boundaries into every other timeline's coordinates
via the group's linear conversion. Each member is unfolded along its
own resolved played spans: a new timeline of the member's **same
concrete type** with one appended child (plus a matching named Region)
per section, in unfolded coordinates.

This is the group-level equivalent of
`timetoalign.timelines.flow.create_unfolded_timeline`, but
applied to every member at once. It shares the append-children
assembly via `unfold_via_flowmap`, so each member's children and
Regions carry the same per-section names as the single-timeline path
(repeats suffixed ``-rend2``, ``-rend3`` …).

#### Parameters {.doc-section .doc-section-parameters}

| Name                  | Type                   | Description                                                                                                                                                                  | Default    |
|-----------------------|------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------|
| flow                  | \'Flow\'               | The computed ``Flow`` (from ``controller.compute_flow()``).                                                                                                                  | _required_ |
| flow_controller       | \'FlowControllerBase\' | The ``FlowControllerBase`` that produced the flow. Required to convert flow sections to quarter-beat coordinates.                                                            | _required_ |
| reference_timeline_id | [str](`str`)           | ID of the timeline whose coordinate space the flow is defined in (typically the score CLT).  Section boundaries are resolved here first, then mapped to all other timelines. | _required_ |
| include_children      | [bool](`bool`)         | Whether to recursively slice child timelines within each section.                                                                                                            | `True`     |
| name                  | [str](`str`) \| None   | Name for the returned group.  Defaults to ``f"{self.name} (unfolded)"``.                                                                                                     | `None`     |

#### Returns {.doc-section .doc-section-returns}

| Name   | Type              | Description                                                            |
|--------|-------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------|
|        | \'TimelineGroup\' | A new ``TimelineGroup`` containing the unfolded timelines. Each        |
|        | \'TimelineGroup\' | member keeps its original timeline ID, is the same concrete type as    |
|        | \'TimelineGroup\' | its source, and carries one appended child and Region per section.     |
|        | \'TimelineGroup\' | A section child is named after its section; its id is minted           |
|        | \'TimelineGroup\' | (``clt_2``, ...), so that timeline ids stay unique across the          |
|        | \'TimelineGroup\' | group.                                                                 |
|        | \'TimelineGroup\' | The reference timeline additionally carries a reverse FlowMap          |
|        | \'TimelineGroup\' | (id ``"source"``) and a forward FlowMap (id ``f"forward_{flow.id}"``). |

#### Raises {.doc-section .doc-section-raises}

| Name   | Type                       | Description                                        |
|--------|----------------------------|----------------------------------------------------|
|        | [KeyError](`KeyError`)     | If ``reference_timeline_id`` is not in the group.  |
|        | [ValueError](`ValueError`) | If the flow controller cannot compute QB sections. |

#### Examples {.doc-section .doc-section-examples}

```python
>>> loader = Ms3Loader.from_file("notes.tsv", "measures.tsv")
>>> controller = loader.create_flow_controller()
>>> flow = controller.compute_flow(FlowMode.default)
>>> score_group = TimelineGroup(
...     id="score", timelines=[clt_1, dgt_1, openscore]
... )
>>> unfolded = score_group.apply_flow(flow, controller, "clt_1")
```

### from_dict { #timetoalign.timelines.TimelineGroup.from_dict }

```python
timelines.TimelineGroup.from_dict(data, *, group_id=None, name=None)
```

Read a group from a TimeSkeleton manifest.

- A manifest of one root timeline and no group makes a group of that
  timeline; *group_id* or *name* (or both) must be given.
- An anonymous manifest with one group reads that group. Arguments
  naming it select it; arguments naming nothing override its id and
  name; given both, they must agree, both naming the group or
  neither.

In these two cases the manifest is read as a whole: its ``meta``,
``graphical`` and unknown keys are kept so that :meth:`to_dict`
writes them back, around the anonymous manifest a group writes.
- From a manifest with several groups, or a named one, *group_id* or
  *name* (or both) must be given and select the one group whose id
  and name match them.

A group is read with the timelines its members need: each member id
is resolved among the manifest's roots and all their descendants, and
the members are added in the group's ``graphical.order`` entry (in
``members`` order without one). ``graphical``'s other keys are kept as
:attr:`styling`, unread, when the manifest is read as a whole. Keys
the library does not know are kept on the object read from the JSON
object they were found in, and written back.

#### Parameters {.doc-section .doc-section-parameters}

| Name     | Type                                                | Description                                            | Default    |
|----------|-----------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------|------------|
| data     | [dict](`dict`)\[[str](`str`), [Any](`typing.Any`)\] | A TimeSkeleton manifest.                               | _required_ |
| group_id | [str](`str`) \| None                                | The group id to select, or the id the group takes.     | `None`     |
| name     | [str](`str`) \| None                                | The group name to select, or the name the group takes. | `None`     |

#### Returns {.doc-section .doc-section-returns}

| Name   | Type                             | Description     |
|--------|----------------------------------|-----------------|
|        | [Self](`typing_extensions.Self`) | The group read. |

#### Raises {.doc-section .doc-section-raises}

| Name   | Type                       | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
|--------|----------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
|        | [ValueError](`ValueError`) | If *data* is no TimeSkeleton manifest of version 0.7.0 or is malformed — a member naming no timeline of the manifest, an order that is no permutation of its group's members, a member that is an ancestor or descendant of another member, a group id held by a timeline or by another group — or if the selection matches no group or several; the message names the problem, or the manifest's groups. |

#### Examples {.doc-section .doc-section-examples}

```python
>>> from fractions import Fraction
>>> from timetoalign.timelines import TimelineGroup
>>> from timetoalign.timelines.types import ContinuousLogicalTimeline
>>> group = TimelineGroup(
...     name="edition",
...     timelines=[ContinuousLogicalTimeline(length=Fraction(8))],
... )
>>> data = group.to_dict()
>>> TimelineGroup.from_dict(data).to_dict() == data
True
```

### get_events { #timetoalign.timelines.TimelineGroup.get_events }

```python
timelines.TimelineGroup.get_events(timeline_id=None, **kwargs)
```

Get events from all timelines in the group, concatenated.

Collects events from all member timelines (or a specific one) and
concatenates their Arrow tables into a single EventData. Each row includes a
``timeline_id`` field identifying the source timeline. A member-provided
``timeline_id`` column is discarded because group membership is authoritative.

#### Parameters {.doc-section .doc-section-parameters}

| Name        | Type                 | Description                                                                                                     | Default   |
|-------------|----------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------|
| timeline_id | [str](`str`) \| None | If provided, only return events from this timeline. Supports partial string and regex matching.                 | `None`    |
| **kwargs    | [Any](`typing.Any`)  | Passed through to each timeline's ``get_events()`` method (e.g., ``min_coord``, ``max_coord``, ``event_type``). | `{}`      |

#### Returns {.doc-section .doc-section-returns}

| Name   | Type                                         | Description                                                       |
|--------|----------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------|
|        | [EventData](`timetoalign.storage.EventData`) | EventData with events from all (or specified) timelines. Includes |
|        | [EventData](`timetoalign.storage.EventData`) | a ``timeline_id`` field and standard event fields (``start``,     |
|        | [EventData](`timetoalign.storage.EventData`) | ``end``, ``event_type``, etc.).                                   |

#### Examples {.doc-section .doc-section-examples}

```python
>>> # Get all events from all timelines
>>> df = group.get_events().to_dataframe()
```

```python
>>> # Get events from a specific timeline
>>> df = group.get_events(timeline_id="clt_1").to_dataframe()
```

```python
>>> # Get events with filters
>>> df = group.get_events(
...     event_type="Note", min_coord=0.0, max_coord=100.0
... ).to_dataframe()
```

### get_timeline { #timetoalign.timelines.TimelineGroup.get_timeline }

```python
timelines.TimelineGroup.get_timeline(timeline_id)
```

Get a timeline by ID.

Supports partial string and regex matching:
1. Exact match: If ``timeline_id`` matches an ID exactly, returns it.
2. Substring match: If ``timeline_id`` is a substring of exactly one ID,
   returns that timeline. If multiple match, returns the first and warns.
3. Regex match: If ``timeline_id`` is a valid regex, matches via
   ``re.search()``. Same first-match logic with warning.

#### Parameters {.doc-section .doc-section-parameters}

| Name        | Type         | Description                                                   | Default    |
|-------------|--------------|---------------------------------------------------------------|------------|
| timeline_id | [str](`str`) | The timeline's unique identifier, or a partial/regex pattern. | _required_ |

#### Returns {.doc-section .doc-section-returns}

| Name   | Type         | Description          |
|--------|--------------|----------------------|
|        | \'Timeline\' | The Timeline object. |

#### Raises {.doc-section .doc-section-raises}

| Name   | Type                   | Description                         |
|--------|------------------------|-------------------------------------|
|        | [KeyError](`KeyError`) | If no timeline matches the pattern. |

#### Examples {.doc-section .doc-section-examples}

```python
>>> group.get_timeline("clt_1")           # Exact match
>>> group.get_timeline("notes")          # Substring match
>>> group.get_timeline(r"^score:")       # Regex match
```

timelines.TimelineGroup.get_timestamp(

Dispatch a positional or event-key timestamp query.

| Name            | Type                                                                                                                                                                                                                        | Description                                        | Default    |
|-----------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------|------------|
| at              | [CoordinateInput](`timetoalign.core.retrieval.CoordinateInput`) \| [CoordinateCollection](`timetoalign.core.retrieval.CoordinateCollection`) \| [str](`str`) \| [KeyCollection](`timetoalign.core.retrieval.KeyCollection`) | Scalar or plural coordinate position or event key. | _required_ |
| timeline_id     | [str](`str`) \| None                                                                                                                                                                                                        | Member axis the query is expressed on.             | `None`     |
| conversion_maps | [ConversionMapsSpec](`timetoalign.core.timestamp.ConversionMapsSpec`)                                                                                                                                                       | Whether C-Maps are reachable through the stamps.   | `True`     |

#### Raises {.doc-section .doc-section-raises}

### get_timestamp_at { #timetoalign.timelines.TimelineGroup.get_timestamp_at }

```python
timelines.TimelineGroup.get_timestamp_at(
    at,
    timeline_id=None,
    *,
    conversion_maps=True,
)
```

Get a TimeStamp at a specific coordinate.

This is the primary coordinate resolution API for TimelineGroup.
Returns a proper TimeStamp object (same as Timeline.get_timestamp_at).
The queried position is written the way the addressed member writes
numbers; every other member's coordinate is the exact linear image of
that position (see :class:`TimelineGroup`), and each member's
descendants are reached through their exact offsets.

#### Parameters {.doc-section .doc-section-parameters}

| Name            | Type                                                                  | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                          | Default    |
|-----------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------|
| at              | [CoordinateSpec](`timetoalign.core.CoordinateSpec`)                   | The query coordinate. Can be: - int/float/Fraction: Raw value, timeline_id required - Coordinate: Value with unit, timeline_id required - IdCoordinate: Value with unit AND timeline_id (timeline_id param optional) | _required_ |
| timeline_id     | [str](`str`) \| None                                                  | Which timeline the coordinate refers to. Required unless coordinate is an IdCoordinate.                                                                                                                              | `None`     |
| conversion_maps | [ConversionMapsSpec](`timetoalign.core.timestamp.ConversionMapsSpec`) | Whether to include C-Map values in timestamp. - True (default): C-Maps accessible through typed getters. - False/None: Only timeline coordinates                                                                     | `True`     |

#### Returns {.doc-section .doc-section-returns}

| Name   | Type                                                | Description                                                          |
|--------|-----------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------|
|        | [TimeStamp](`timetoalign.core.timestamp.TimeStamp`) | TimeStamp with axis set to the input coordinate and source_id set to |
|        | [TimeStamp](`timetoalign.core.timestamp.TimeStamp`) | the timeline. Access other timelines via `get_coordinate_for()`.     |
|        | [TimeStamp](`timetoalign.core.timestamp.TimeStamp`) | Access C-Maps via `get_unit()` or `get_conversion_for()`. The        |
|        | [TimeStamp](`timetoalign.core.timestamp.TimeStamp`) | stamp is interpolated unless the position is the group's common      |
|        | [TimeStamp](`timetoalign.core.timestamp.TimeStamp`) | start or end.                                                        |

#### Raises {.doc-section .doc-section-raises}

| Name   | Type                                                                  | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
|--------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
|        | [KeyError](`KeyError`)                                                | If timeline_id is not in the group.                                                                                                                                                                             |
|        | [UnknownLengthError](`timetoalign.timelines.base.UnknownLengthError`) | If a position must be converted between two members and either length is unknown. A member of unknown length bounds its positions below only, so a group of that member alone answers every position from 0 on. |
|        | [ValueError](`ValueError`)                                            | If coordinate is outside the timeline's range in the group.                                                                                                                                                     |
|        | [ValueError](`ValueError`)                                            | If timeline_id is None and coordinate is not IdCoordinate.                                                                                                                                                      |

#### Examples {.doc-section .doc-section-examples}

```python
>>> from timetoalign.core import IdCoordinate, TimeUnit
>>> from timetoalign.timelines import TimelineGroup
>>> from timetoalign.timelines.types import (
...     ContinuousPhysicalTimeline,
...     DiscreteGraphicalTimeline,
... )
>>> dgt_1 = DiscreteGraphicalTimeline(length=4875, unit="pixels")
>>> audio = ContinuousPhysicalTimeline(length=150.0, unit="seconds")
>>> group = TimelineGroup(timelines=[dgt_1, audio])
```

```python
>>> ts = group.get_timestamp_at(75.0, "cpt_1")
>>> ts.axis
IdCoordinate(75.0, seconds, 'cpt_1')
>>> ts.get_coordinate_for("dgt_1", format="int")
2438
```

```python
>>> # Using IdCoordinate (timeline_id extracted automatically)
>>> coord = IdCoordinate(75.0, TimeUnit.seconds, "cpt_1")
>>> group.get_timestamp_at(coord).axis
IdCoordinate(75.0, seconds, 'cpt_1')
```

### get_timestamp_for { #timetoalign.timelines.TimelineGroup.get_timestamp_for }

```python
timelines.TimelineGroup.get_timestamp_for(
    key,
    timeline_id=None,
    *,
    conversion_maps=True,
)
```

Get the TimeStamp for a specific event by its ID.

Searches all timelines in the group for the event and returns
the corresponding TimeStamp (same structure as
Timeline.get_timestamp_at).

#### Parameters {.doc-section .doc-section-parameters}

| Name            | Type                                                                  | Description                                                                         | Default    |
|-----------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------|
| key             | [str](`str`)                                                          | The event's unique identifier.                                                      | _required_ |
| timeline_id     | [str](`str`) \| None                                                  | Member whose axis the stamp is anchored on; by default the member owning the event. | `None`     |
| conversion_maps | [ConversionMapsSpec](`timetoalign.core.timestamp.ConversionMapsSpec`) | Whether C-Maps are reachable through the stamp.                                     | `True`     |

#### Returns {.doc-section .doc-section-returns}

| Name   | Type                                                | Description                                                       |
|--------|-----------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------|
|        | [TimeStamp](`timetoalign.core.timestamp.TimeStamp`) | TimeStamp at the event's coordinate, with access to all           |
|        | [TimeStamp](`timetoalign.core.timestamp.TimeStamp`) | timelines via `get_coordinate_for()` and C-Maps via `get_unit()`. |

#### Raises {.doc-section .doc-section-raises}

| Name   | Type                   | Description                                |
|--------|------------------------|--------------------------------------------|
|        | [KeyError](`KeyError`) | If the event is not found in any timeline. |

#### Examples {.doc-section .doc-section-examples}

```python
>>> from timetoalign.timelines import TimelineGroup
>>> from timetoalign.timelines.types import ContinuousPhysicalTimeline
>>> audio = ContinuousPhysicalTimeline(length=150.0, unit="seconds", uid="audio")
>>> audio.add_events([{"event_type": "Note", "instant": 45.5}])
>>> group = TimelineGroup(id="my_group", timelines=[audio])
```

```python
>>> ts = group.get_timestamp_for("note:000001")
>>> ts.get_coordinate_for("audio", format="float")
45.5
>>> ts.get_unit(TimeUnit.seconds)  # C-Map conversion
IdCoordinate(45.5, seconds, 'audio')
```

### get_timestamp_table { #timetoalign.timelines.TimelineGroup.get_timestamp_table }

```python
timelines.TimelineGroup.get_timestamp_table(
    at=None,
    timeline_id=None,
    *,
    timeline_filter=None,
    conversion_maps=True,
    format='table',
    fields=None,
    units=None,
)
```

Get the group's timestamps as a table, one row per cross-section.

#### Parameters {.doc-section .doc-section-parameters}

| Name            | Type                                                                                                                                                                                                                                | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      | Default   |
|-----------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------|
| at              | [CoordinateInput](`timetoalign.core.retrieval.CoordinateInput`) \| [CoordinateCollection](`timetoalign.core.retrieval.CoordinateCollection`) \| [str](`str`) \| [KeyCollection](`timetoalign.core.retrieval.KeyCollection`) \| None | Positions or event IDs to tabulate, one row each in input order. If None, the rows are the group's two stored timestamps: the common start and the common end, each member at ``0`` and at its length, exact in its declared number type.                        | `None`    |
| timeline_id     | [str](`str`) \| None                                                                                                                                                                                                                | Which timeline the positions refer to. Required for entries without an embedded timeline ID.                                                                                                                                                                     | `None`    |
| timeline_filter | [set](`set`)\[[str](`str`)\] \| None                                                                                                                                                                                                | Only include these timeline fields.                                                                                                                                                                                                                              | `None`    |
| conversion_maps | [ConversionMapsSpec](`timetoalign.core.timestamp.ConversionMapsSpec`)                                                                                                                                                               | Whether to include C-Map fields from member timelines. - True (default): Include all attached C-Maps from all timelines - False/None: No C-Map fields                                                                                                            | `True`    |
| format          | [TableFormat](`timetoalign.core.retrieval.TableFormat`)                                                                                                                                                                             | ``"table"`` (default) for a PyArrow table, ``"dataframe"`` for a pandas DataFrame.                                                                                                                                                                               | `'table'` |
| fields          | \'ColumnNaming \| Callable\[\[str, dict\], str\] \| list\[str\] \| None\'                                                                                                                                                           | How to name the DataFrame fields (``format="dataframe"``): - None or ColumnNaming.name (default): Use timeline/cmap name - ColumnNaming.id: Use timeline/cmap id - Callable: Function taking (name, metadata_dict) -> new_name - list[str]: Explicit field names | `None`    |
| units           | [bool](`bool`) \| None                                                                                                                                                                                                              | If True (the DataFrame default), append units to field names like "name (unit)".                                                                                                                                                                                 | `None`    |

#### Returns {.doc-section .doc-section-returns}

| Name   | Type                                                                                       | Description                                                      |
|--------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------|
|        | [pa](`pyarrow`).[Table](`pyarrow.Table`) \| [pd](`pandas`).[DataFrame](`pandas.DataFrame`) | One row per timestamp and one field per timeline — coordinate    |
|        | [pa](`pyarrow`).[Table](`pyarrow.Table`) \| [pd](`pandas`).[DataFrame](`pandas.DataFrame`) | structs carrying each number twice — plus C-Map fields when      |
|        | [pa](`pyarrow`).[Table](`pyarrow.Table`) \| [pd](`pandas`).[DataFrame](`pandas.DataFrame`) | ``conversion_maps`` is enabled. An empty group gives an empty    |
|        | [pa](`pyarrow`).[Table](`pyarrow.Table`) \| [pd](`pandas`).[DataFrame](`pandas.DataFrame`) | table.                                                           |
|        | [pa](`pyarrow`).[Table](`pyarrow.Table`) \| [pd](`pandas`).[DataFrame](`pandas.DataFrame`) | A null cell means one thing only: that timeline does not reach   |
|        | [pa](`pyarrow`).[Table](`pyarrow.Table`) \| [pd](`pandas`).[DataFrame](`pandas.DataFrame`) | that position. An unresolvable *query* position is an error, not |
|        | [pa](`pyarrow`).[Table](`pyarrow.Table`) \| [pd](`pandas`).[DataFrame](`pandas.DataFrame`) | a null, so the two can never be confused.                        |

#### Raises {.doc-section .doc-section-raises}

| Name   | Type                       | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
|--------|----------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
|        | [KeyError](`KeyError`)     | If a named timeline is not in the group.                                                                                                                                                                                              |
|        | [ValueError](`ValueError`) | On an unknown ``format``, when a DataFrame-shaping option is supplied for an Arrow result, or when a queried position lies outside its timeline's range. A batch answers completely or not at all, on this lane as on the stamp lane. |

#### Examples {.doc-section .doc-section-examples}

```python
>>> from fractions import Fraction
>>> from timetoalign.timelines import TimelineGroup
>>> from timetoalign.timelines.types import (
...     ContinuousLogicalTimeline,
...     ContinuousPhysicalTimeline,
...     DiscreteGraphicalTimeline,
... )
>>> pixels = DiscreteGraphicalTimeline(length=4000, unit="pixels")
>>> audio = ContinuousPhysicalTimeline(length=10.0, unit="seconds")
>>> group = TimelineGroup(timelines=[pixels, audio])
>>> group.get_timestamp_table().column_names
['dgt_1', 'cpt_1']
>>> group.get_timestamp_table([0.0, 2.5], "cpt_1", format="dataframe")
   dgt_1 (pixels)  cpt_1 (seconds)
0               0              0.0
1            1000              2.5
```

The stored rows are exact:

```python
>>> score = ContinuousLogicalTimeline(length=Fraction(5, 3))
>>> TimelineGroup(timelines=[score]).get_timestamp_table(
...     format="dataframe"
... )["clt_1 (quarters)"].tolist()
[Fraction(0, 1), Fraction(5, 3)]
```

### get_timestamps_at { #timetoalign.timelines.TimelineGroup.get_timestamps_at }

```python
timelines.TimelineGroup.get_timestamps_at(
    at,
    timeline_id=None,
    *,
    conversion_maps=True,
)
```

Get TimeStamps at a collection of coordinates, in input order.

#### Parameters {.doc-section .doc-section-parameters}

| Name            | Type                                                                      | Description                                                                                                                    | Default    |
|-----------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------|
| at              | [CoordinateCollection](`timetoalign.core.retrieval.CoordinateCollection`) | Coordinate positions to query.                                                                                                 | _required_ |
| timeline_id     | [str](`str`) \| None                                                      | Which timeline the coordinates refer to. Required for entries without an embedded timeline ID.                                 | `None`     |
| conversion_maps | [ConversionMapsSpec](`timetoalign.core.timestamp.ConversionMapsSpec`)     | Whether C-Maps are reachable through the stamps. - True (default): all attached C-Maps - False/None: only timeline coordinates | `True`     |

#### Returns {.doc-section .doc-section-returns}

| Name   | Type                                                                  | Description                                                      |
|--------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------|
|        | [list](`list`)\[[TimeStamp](`timetoalign.core.timestamp.TimeStamp`)\] | One TimeStamp per input coordinate; an empty collection gives an |
|        | [list](`list`)\[[TimeStamp](`timetoalign.core.timestamp.TimeStamp`)\] | empty list.                                                      |

#### Raises {.doc-section .doc-section-raises}

| Name   | Type                       | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
|--------|----------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
|        | [KeyError](`KeyError`)     | If a named timeline is not in the group.                                                                                                                                                                                  |
|        | [ValueError](`ValueError`) | If a position lies outside its timeline's range, or a raw value arrives without a ``timeline_id``. A plural query answers completely or not at all — one unresolvable position raises rather than yielding a partial row. |

#### Examples {.doc-section .doc-section-examples}

```python
>>> from timetoalign.timelines import TimelineGroup
>>> from timetoalign.timelines.types import (
...     ContinuousPhysicalTimeline,
...     DiscreteGraphicalTimeline,
... )
>>> pixels = DiscreteGraphicalTimeline(length=4000, unit="pixels", uid="dgt_1")
>>> audio = ContinuousPhysicalTimeline(length=10.0, unit="seconds", uid="cpt_1")
>>> group = TimelineGroup(id="pair", timelines=[pixels, audio])
>>> stamps = group.get_timestamps_at([0.0, 2.5], "cpt_1")
>>> [stamp.get_coordinate_for("dgt_1", format="int") for stamp in stamps]
[0, 1000]
```

#### See Also {.doc-section .doc-section-see-also}

get_timestamp_table: The same batch as one table or DataFrame.

### to_dict { #timetoalign.timelines.TimelineGroup.to_dict }

```python
timelines.TimelineGroup.to_dict(
    minimal=False,
    events=False,
    external_references=False,
)
```

Write an anonymous TimeSkeleton manifest holding this group.

The group is written with every timeline it needs: ``"timelines"``
holds the root of each member's tree — a member that is a child
contributes its root, which holds it — each a timeline object as
:meth:`Timeline.to_dict <timetoalign.timelines.Timeline.to_dict>`
writes it, sorted by id. ``"groups"`` holds the group, naming its
members by id, sorted; ``graphical.order`` keeps their display
order, which is the order they were added in, under the group's id,
beside the members of :attr:`styling`. A group read from a manifest
as a whole writes that manifest's ``meta`` and unknown keys back.

#### Parameters {.doc-section .doc-section-parameters}

| Name                | Type           | Description                                        | Default   |
|---------------------|----------------|----------------------------------------------------|-----------|
| minimal             | [bool](`bool`) | If True, leave out every key at its default value. | `False`   |
| events              | [bool](`bool`) | Write every timeline's event rows.                 | `False`   |
| external_references | [bool](`bool`) | Write every timeline's external references.        | `False`   |

#### Returns {.doc-section .doc-section-returns}

| Name   | Type                                                | Description                                                    |
|--------|-----------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------|
|        | [dict](`dict`)\[[str](`str`), [Any](`typing.Any`)\] | ``{"timeskeleton": "0.7.0", ..., "timelines": [...], "groups": |
|        | [dict](`dict`)\[[str](`str`), [Any](`typing.Any`)\] | [{"id", "name", "meta", "members"}], "graphical": {"order":    |
|        | [dict](`dict`)\[[str](`str`), [Any](`typing.Any`)\] | {group id: [...]}, ...}}``.                                    |

#### Examples {.doc-section .doc-section-examples}

```python
>>> from fractions import Fraction
>>> from timetoalign.timelines import TimelineGroup
>>> from timetoalign.timelines.types import (
...     ContinuousLogicalTimeline,
...     DiscreteGraphicalTimeline,
... )
>>> image = DiscreteGraphicalTimeline(length=5000)
>>> part = DiscreteGraphicalTimeline(length=2000)
>>> image.add_child(part, offset=1000)
>>> group = TimelineGroup(
...     timelines=[part, ContinuousLogicalTimeline(length=Fraction(8))]
... )
>>> data = group.to_dict(minimal=True)
>>> [timeline["id"] for timeline in data["timelines"]]
['clt_1', 'dgt_1']
>>> data["groups"]
[{'id': 'group_1', 'members': ['clt_1', 'dgt_2']}]
>>> data["graphical"]
{'order': {'group_1': ['dgt_2', 'clt_1']}}
```
